items: Walk through the phases of a structured solution design process.
Distinguish requirements gathering from evaluation and documentation.
Explain how prototyping and feedback loops reduce risk.
Connect the design process back to the SA's multiple working roles.
Design Process — a repeatable sequence from understanding the problem to validating the solution.
Requirements (functional & non-functional) — what the system must do vs. how well it must do it.
NFR — non-functional requirements: performance, security, scalability, compliance.
Proof of Concept (POC) — a small build to validate a risky assumption.
Iterative refinement — revisiting the design as new constraints appear.

blocks.text: A disciplined design process keeps an SA from jumping to a solution before understanding the problem. The typical flow is: (1) Understand the context and stakeholders, (2) Gather and classify requirements, (3) Explore and evaluate options, (4) Produce the design and documentation, (5) Validate with a POC or prototype, and (6) Review, govern, and iterate.

The SA collects functional requirements (features) and non-functional requirements (NFRs: latency, throughput, security, compliance, cost ceiling). As a Business Analyst / Product Owner the SA manages the backlog; as a Technical Leader they ensure NFRs and security governance are explicit rather than assumed.

Options are compared against the Well-Architected pillars. Trade-offs are surfaced and documented. The SA, acting as Technical Consultant, produces cost and effort estimations so the business can choose knowingly.

High-level design (components, boundaries, data flow) is followed by low-level design (interfaces, schemas, sequences). A POC de-risks the hardest assumption — a new technology, a scaling limit, an integration. Feedback loops bring the design back to stakeholders. Finally, the SA governs the design through reviews and keeps documentation alive as the system evolves.
